clue.text: A tricky puzzle in Bert's area?

definitions.text: A tricky puzzle in Bert's area?

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the letters of the phrase after it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a puzzle set in Bert's part of town is a hard one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges INBERTSAREA, the letters of 'in Bert's area', and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult puzzle or riddle that taxes the mind is called by this name.

clue.text: Begin to read poem — or start the show?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word read is all that is wanted here

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: the start of the word or gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A performer wonders whether to open the show by reading a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin to' takes R from 'read' and 'start' takes O from 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy exhibition of bronco riding and roping is a kind of public show.

clue.text: Base one? Good lord!

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a lord is a noble, a member of the peerage

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at someone's base behaviour: Good lord!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is an adjective meaning dishonourable, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and dishonourable conduct is mean and unworthy, the opposite of honourable.

clue.text: Pulling in the direction of the flank

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
a flank of an army or building is a wing

explanation.surface: Something is being dragged towards one side of a formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauling a vehicle or boat behind on a rope is drawing it along.

clue.text: One doubts a rough costing

indicators.note: a rough version is unpolished and muddled, so the letters of costing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sceptical of an approximate price estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges 'costing' to GNOSTIC, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds that God's existence cannot be known is a doubter in matters of faith.

clue.text: Large bird delayed copy

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late means delayed or behind time

explanation.surface: A big bird is late, and so is a copy of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copy' is a verb, imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone, striving to match them, is to follow their example.

clue.text: Game provoked by royal mail strike?

definitions.meaning: a party kissing game in which a player pretends to deliver letters
Royal Mail is the British postal service; strike here means a knock at the door, not industrial action

explanation.surface: A game is said to have been sparked off by a walkout of Britain's postal workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' reads as industrial action but means a blow, the rap on the door made by the letter-carrier. Royal Mail is the UK's national postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party pastime involving kisses, and literally the rap at the door made by a mail deliverer.

clue.text: Confessed to have granted access

definitions.meaning: owned up to something, acknowledged guilt
allowed someone to enter, let in

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having let a person in.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up to a fault and letting someone enter are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: Where to eat in ecstasy?

parts.note: ecstasy can be called transport, rapture, so a place to eat in it is a roadside eatery for lorry drivers

explanation.surface: A question about a blissful place to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport is an old word for rapture, so the eatery is one 'in transport'; a British roadside cafe for lorry drivers goes by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap roadside eating place used mainly by lorry drivers on British trunk roads.

clue.text: Liverpool denial revealed, as of times gone by

indicators.note: revealed shows that the letters sit visibly inside the words Liverpool denial

explanation.surface: Someone from Liverpool denies something about the past, and the truth comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' exposes the run inside 'LiverpoOL DENial'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adjective for bygone days, long ago.

clue.text: Failed to see what the limbo dancer did

definitions.meaning: collapsed, as a business does when it goes bust
a limbo dancer passes beneath a low bar

explanation.surface: A limbo dancer's routine is described as a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that went bust collapsed, and a limbo dancer passed beneath the bar.

clue.text: The instruments of mobster on display

indicators.note: putting something on display arranges it for show, so the letters of mobster on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangster's weapons, perhaps his instruments of trade, are laid out for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges MOBSTERON, the letters of 'mobster on'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass instruments with a sliding tube are a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Strange tale swallowed by a number

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken in by, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: N is used in algebra for an unspecified number
a tale is a lie, a made-up story

explanation.surface: An odd story has been absorbed by a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts LIE inside A plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreign and unfamiliar is outlandish or odd.

clue.text: Worker on the edge of song

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A labourer stands at the very brink of breaking into song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing hymn of praise or national loyalty is a type of song.

clue.text: Insignificant affair following short trip

indicators.note: following means the affair comes after the shortened trip
short means the word trip is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

explanation.surface: A minor romance came after a quick journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops P from 'trip' to leave TRI, and 'following' puts FLING after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something petty and unimportant is of trivial consequence.

clue.text: Avoid team with pace

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a step is a pace

explanation.surface: Advice to a footballer: dodge the opposition by moving quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge an issue or blow is to evade it by moving aside.

clue.text: A noted writer

parts.note: noted reads as famous but means writing in musical notes, so this is someone who writes music

explanation.surface: A celebrated author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' suggests famous, but here it means one who writes in notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes music sets it down in notes.

clue.text: Sloppy mistakes by brick carrier

parts.note: slips are small errors
a hod is a trough on a pole for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A careless builder's labourer keeps making errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless and untidy work is done in a slapdash way.

clue.text: Honest, but otherwise recognised no god

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters left are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An honest person admits, contrary to what was assumed, that they acknowledged no deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G, O and D from 'recognised', and 'otherwise' rearranges what is left, RECNISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and truthful feelings are heartfelt and free of pretence.

clue.text: Make an offer for supply ship

definitions.meaning: to bid formally for a contract
a vessel that ferries stores to larger ships

explanation.surface: Someone bids for a contract to provide a stores vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal bid for work, and a small boat that serves a larger vessel with provisions.

clue.text: Moral — there's no art in poor theatrical…

indicators.note: poor suggests the word is in bad shape, so its remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A moral judgement: there's no artistry in a bad dramatic performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes A, R and T out of 'theatrical', and 'poor' rearranges the rest, THEICAL. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct that is principled and right is in line with good conduct.

clue.text: …county; act right with group

parts.note: to do is to act
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Continuing the theatre theme: a county stages a play correctly with a company.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural shire in south-west England, one of the English counties.

clue.text: Material gain, say — all go in at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gain, then urges everyone to join in at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes the final letters of 'gain, say, all, go, in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric used for stockings and ropes is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Portentous support he half ticked off

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: half of the word ticked is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A supporter's half-finished ticking of boxes seems ominous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TIC, the first half of 'ticked'; 'off' rounds out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Foretelling events ominously, something predictive is full of foreboding.

clue.text: Fruit at last ready for picking? Rubbish

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of fruit

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to be picked

explanation.surface: A grower asks whether the fruit is finally ripe enough to harvest, then calls it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes T from 'Fruit'. Tripe is also cow's stomach eaten in Britain, hence its slang sense of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless talk is slang for garbage.

clue.text: Tory population count vocally in agreement

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: vocally means the word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population

explanation.surface: Conservatives counting people out loud find they all agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocally' turns CENSUS into the sound-alike SENSUS. Tory means a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: General accord among a group is a shared view all accept.

clue.text: Main source of inspiration in cook

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for cook

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The key thing that inspires a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes I from 'inspiration' and 'in' puts it inside CHEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Main as an adjective means principal or most important.

clue.text: Streaker led off with hat

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naked runner leads the way, wearing nothing but a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges STREAKERLED, the letters of 'Streaker led'. The hat is the peaked cap associated with Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth cap with peaks front and back and ear flaps, worn for hunting deer.
